stem: A member of a Parliament or a State Legislature can be elected as President, but

stem: Under which article of the Indian Constitution can the President be impeached?
solution: The President of India can be impeached under Article 61 of the Constitution of India: Procedure: The procedure for impeachment is outlined in Article 61. Initiation: Either House of Parliament can initiate impeachment charges. Requirements: To initiate impeachment, at least a quarter of the members of the House must sign the charges, and the President must be given 14 days’ notice. Passage: The resolution must pass by a two-thirds majority in both Houses of Parliament. Removal: Once the resolution passes, the President is impeached and removed from office.

solution: The first national emergency was declared in India on 26 October 1962 during the India–China war. This was a conflict between the two countries over their disputed border. The Chinese army launched a full-scale invasion of India, which caught the Indian military and government by surprise. The Indian government declared a state of national emergency in response to the conflict. During the emergency, the government had increased powers to control the media and censorship, as well as the ability to detain individuals without trial. The emergency was officially revoked 21 months later on 10 January 1968. Additional Information: National Emergency in India has been declared 3 times – 1962 (China war), 1971 (Pakistan war), and 1975 (Internal Disturbances). National Emergency can be proclaimed by the President when he/she perceives threats to the nation from internal and external sources or from financial situations of crisis. National emergency is mentioned in the Article 352.

solution: The abundance of plankton in the ocean is shaped by several key factors: Depth of water: Phytoplankton, which rely on sunlight for photosynthesis, are most abundant in the sunlit upper layers of the ocean, known as the photic zone. solution: After his release from prison in 1924, Gandhi sought to bring back the Swarajists to the Congress and re-unite the party. Gandhi’s supporters were in a vast majority in the Congress, and the Congress still remained India’s largest political party, but Gandhi felt it necessary to heal the divide with the warajists, so as to heal the nation’s wounds over the 1922 suspension. The Swarajists sought more representation in the Congress offices, and an end to the andatory requirement for Congressmen to spin khadi cloth and do social service as a rerequisite for office.. This was opposed by Gandhi’s supporters, men like Vallabhbhai Patel, Jawaharlal Nehru and Rajendra Prasad, who became known as the No Changers as opposed to the Swarajist changers. Gandhi relaxed the rules on spinning and named some Swarajists to important positions in the congress party. He also encouraged the Congress to support those Swarajists elected to the councils, so as not to embarrass them and leave them rudderless before the British authorities.

stem: When a mass m is hung on a spring, the spring stretched by 6 cm. If the loaded spring is pulled downward a little and released, then the period of vibration of the system will be:

subject: Physics
stem: When X-rays are produced:
optA: heat is generated at the target.
optB: heat is absorbed at the target.
optC: the temperature of the target remains constant.
optD: brilliant light is seen at the target.
solution: When X-rays are produced in an X-ray tube, high-energy electrons are accelerated and directed towards a target, typically made of tungsten. Upon impact, the electrons’ kinetic energy is converted into two forms: X-rays and heat. The conversion efficiency is such that around 99% of the energy is transformed into heat, while only a small fraction is emitted as X-rays. Due to the substantial heat produced, the target material must possess a high melting point to endure the thermal energy. This is why materials like tungsten, known for their high melting points, are commonly used as targets in X-ray tubes.

subject: Chemistry
stem: What is the colour of oxygen in solid state?
solution: Solid oxygen is clear and has a light sky-blue colour because it absorbs red light in the visible light spectrum. This colour is due to electronic transitions from the triplet ground state to the singlet ground state. Temperature: Oxygen becomes solid at temperatures below –218.79oC. Liquid oxygen is also pale blue in colour and is extremely cold. It is non-flammable but is a strong oxidiser.

solution: The site of ribosome formation in a living cell is nucleolus. Ribosomes are small particles found in the cytoplasm of cells, attached to the endoplasmic reticulum, and they are responsible for protein synthesis.

subject: Biology
stem: Who are the first time saw bacteria through a microscope made by himself?
solution: Anton Van Leeuwenhoek was the first person to observe bacteria through a microscope he made himself: Discovery: Leeuwenhoek used a single-lens microscope to observe bacteria and protozoa. He mixed plaque from his teeth with water and saw what he called “many very little living animalcules.” Contributions: Leeuwenhoek is known as the father of microbiology.
